author: R. W. Bauer
title: John Kennedy highlights local outreach efforts and foreign policy views in recent tweets
text:
Senator John Kennedy, a Republican from Louisiana, used his social media platform to inform constituents about local events and share opinions on international affairs and legislative developments in a series of tweets posted between May 12 and May 13, 2026.
On May 12, Kennedy addressed Louisiana residents regarding an upcoming event: “Friends in Louisiana: I wanted you to hear about an event my office and our local passport agency are hosting in Lafayette Parish on Thursday, May 21. I hope it’s helpful to any Louisianians who need to apply for or renew their passports ahead of travel plans.”
Later the same day, Kennedy commented on international security concerns involving China and the United Kingdom’s shared military base with the United States: “If you turned President Xi Jinping upside down and shook him, Mauritius would fall out of his pocket. We cannot let the UK hand over our shared military base on Diego Garcia to China’s BFF.” The tweet referenced strategic worries over potential changes in control at Diego Garcia, a key U.S.-UK military facility.
On May 13, Kennedy reported progress on one of his legislative initiatives: “My resolution to stop senators’ pay during government shutdowns cleared a key procedural vote today, moving it one step closer to final passage. Fair-minded Americans know senators should feel the pain of a shutdown with the American people.”
Kennedy holds degrees from Vanderbilt University, the University of Virginia School of Law, and Oxford University ( official website ). He serves as ranking member on subcommittees related to energy and economic policy ( official website ) and is active on Senate committees overseeing appropriations, banking, budget issues, and judiciary matters ( official website ). In addition to his legislative work, Kennedy has contributed as an adjunct professor and substitute teacher ( official website ) and authored works on constitutional law as well as state liability statutes ( official website ). He also held leadership roles during his academic career at Vanderbilt University ( official website ).
summary: Senator John Kennedy, a Republican from Louisiana, used his social media platform to inform constituents about local events and share opinions on international affairs and legislative developments in a series of tweets posted between May 12 and May 13, 2026.
